newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 19.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.

LONDON - Europe's biggest telecommunications companies are racing to increase their Internet access business while competing with the Internet by expanding their own online services, says Datamonitor, a research consultancy. Companies like France Telecom, Belgium's Belgacom and BT have failed to use their dominant local telecoms positions to achieve Internet access control, it says. (Reuter)

MADRID - Audiovisual Sport says CanalSatelite, which holds exclusive pay-TV rights to view Spain's premier soccer matches, is ready to talk about sharing those rights with rival digital platform Via Digital. Telefonica de Espana, which leads Via Digital, recently bought control of a 40-percent stake in Audiovisual Sport to gain access to its soccer broadcast rights. (Reuter)

PARIS - As World Youth Days, a biennial Roman Catholic youth festival, opens in Paris, the French Catholic Church is connecting to the Internet. There is the JMJ site specially launched for the event and the Dominicans have launched a site called Jubilatio. A "religious" cyber cafe has just opened in Paris. (Les Echos)
LOS ANGELES - Most information technology companies are committed to a common standard for developing three-dimensional images on the Internet. (La Tribune)

PARIS - Fashion television arrives in the capital of fashion. Last May saw the launch of Fashion TV, broadcasting 24-hour fashion shows on French digital satellite services TPS and CanalSatellite. Investment is minimal since the fashion houses supply the TV pictures, and there is no commmentary. (Liberation)

PARIS - The Amaury press group plans to launch a TV sports news channel using the expertise of its daily sports newspaper L'Equipe and Amaury Sports Organisation, its unit that organises sporting events. (Reuters)

PARIS - The Bordeaux wine harvest began on Monday more than a month earlier than usual, a once-in-a-century event that could yield 1997 vintage wines of exceptionally good quality, growers say. (Reuter)

PARIS - Europe's portable phone makers are cooperating on defining the technological norms for the next generation of phones, to be multimedia portables, expected to come out in the year 2002. (Les Echos)
PARIS - French hypermarket chain Auchan opens its first outlet in Mexico and plans a second store in Mexico and a first in Argentina soon. (Les Echos)

PARIS - The holiday weekend of August 15 was exceptionally good for the Cote d'Azur's hotels and restaurants. St Tropez's hotel occupancy was 100 percent last weekend and has been at 80 percent for the last three weeks. Toulone's tourist office had to put up some tourists in a caravan. (Les Echos)
